Source record: docs/studies/analysis/pulsechain_portal_pricing_20260930.md.
PulseChain Portal backing, aDAI index and local arbitrage
Scope and conclusion
All observed state in this study is from PulseChain, chain ID 369, at block 27,673,486, hash 
0x2702410507da0c8e4bf66c752465d28cc977725a128b9eb405a21f99c29ce9b3. No Ethereum state is substituted for the
copied contracts. Requests were reads; no transactions were signed or broadcast and no configuration
was changed.
Remote backing and local unbacked accounting are compatible. A source-backed bridge can still call
destination mintUnbacked: the destination has issued its own aT oken before receiving its own underlying.
Aave's liquidity index does not multiply new issuance into extra principal. A static waDAI share
represents multiple current aDAI units, which must be normalized before comparing prices.
Existing waDAI has a small quoted PulseX-to-Balancer spread at this block. The tested cycle is
uneconomic even against the base transaction gas minimum at the sampled fee and spot conversion.
New Portal issuance and wrapping also encounter distinct current configuration gates. These findings
specify what would need to change for the proposed route; they do not disprove every possible
coordinated route or establish an operating pARB source bridge.
1. Source backing and destination accounting
Suppose the operator controls a backed source Aave position. Locking or surrendering that position can
secure a bridge's obligation. It does not put pDAI into the PulseChain destination reserve. If the
destination operation creates its exact aDAI through mintUnbacked, it records a local advance until 
backUnbacked delivers underlying there. This remains true even with sound remote backing. The bridge
must prevent the same source claim being spent twice.
This distinction is explicit in the upstream deBridge Portal proposal: the proposed adapter locks liquidity
on one chain, waits for finality, and calls mintUnbacked on the other. This is a design reference, not
evidence that this adapter operates on PulseChain. Aave's Portal architecture provides a credit facility for
integrated bridges; it is not itself a universal token transporter.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 321

Destination operation New Portal unbacked issuance? Requirement
Authorized mintUnbacked Yes Bridge authorization, reserve
validation and sufficient unbacked cap
when called
Deliver pDAI and use ordinary Aave 
supply
No Actual destination underlying and
ordinary supply checks
Transfer existing destination aDAI No A funded holder or relayer and
transferable receipts
Bridge a remote receipt into a
separate representation
Not inherently Exact mapping and a buyer, lender or
adapter accepting that representation
The last three are alternatives to Portal credit, not hidden alternative Portal mint methods. A separate
bridged receipt does not become the existing destination aDAI solely because its symbol matches. 
backUnbacked settles outstanding local advances; it is not an unrestricted way to mint aT okens for the
payer.
2. Five quantities that must remain distinct
Quantity PulseChain result Meaning
DAI normalized liquidity index 9.984280942428067601829364415 Multiplier from scaled aDAI balance to
current aDAI balance
aDAI displayed total supply 400,036,132.903002514218870593 Already includes the index
aDAI scaled total supply 40,066,594.200394977560121344 Internal accounting units before index
multiplication
waDAI.convertToAssets(1e18) 9.956311649989486401 aDAI/pDAI accounting units
represented by one static share
waDAI.convertToShares(1e18) 0.100438800547294637 Static shares for one current asset
unit, as a conversion calculation
The aDAI implementation's _mintScaled divides a new principal amount by the current index before
minting scaled units. Its displayed balance multiplies scaled units by that index. Ignoring rounding and
intervening accrual:
new scaled units = principal / index
new displayed aDAI = new scaled units × index = principal
Therefore, minting 100 current aDAI does not create about 998 current aDAI. A permitted wrapper
conversion would yield about 10.0438800547 waDAI shares. A price near ten pDAI for one waDAI share
would then approximately match the principal represented; it would not establish a tenfold arbitrage
profit.
The underlying DAI oracle returns 1.00009178 in its inherited USD accounting convention. The source's 
latestRoundData.updatedAt is 10 May 2023, 21:39:47 UTC. That stale copied feed is not a current
PulseChain dollar price. Direct oracle requests for these aDAI and waDAI addresses revert, and their
configured price-source addresses are zero. The reserve's underlying valuation, receipt conversion and
exchange price are separate observations.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 322

3. Actual sampled markets and a bounded cycle
The exact V3 aDAI/pDAI PulseX V2 pair has stored reserves of approximately 28,276.614 aDAI and
16,326.380 pDAI: 0.577381 pDAI per aDAI before fee and size effects. A one-aDAI input gives a
reserve-only estimate of 0.575686 pDAI after the pair's 0.29% swap fee. The live aDAI balance is
28,276.789776, slightly above stored reserves because the receipt accrues; this estimate is not a
complete swap simulation. These reads establish a discount in this exact pair, not a several-fold
premium for this aDAI.
The waDAI/pDAI pair holds approximately 31.873622 waDAI and 81.139352 pDAI, giving 2.545658 pDAI
per whole waDAI. That is a premium to one pDAI token, but a discount to the share's approximately
9.956312-unit accounting claim.
An existing-wrapper cycle avoids creating a new wrapper position:
pDAI → buy existing waDAI on PulseX → sell waDAI into Balancer → pDAI
Step Pinned calculation or read
Buy 0.005021940027364730 existing waDAI 0.012823345760635207 pDAI, reserve-based exact-output
calculation
Sell that amount to the DAI linear pool 0.049999500004999931 pDAI, direct queryBatchSwap result
Difference before gas 0.037176154244364724 pDAI
Difference at sampled pDAI/WPLS spot ratio 6.80782566003938 PLS
Gas this difference could fund at sampled base fee 15,733.232 gas
That gas allowance is below the ordinary 21,000 gas transaction minimum, before either swap,
calldata or priority fees. Thus this tested standalone cycle is not profitable at the sampled base fee and
spot conversion. A full executor transaction was not simulated. The calculation does not establish
profitability of a larger or batched route, which would require its own quotes, incremental gas and
closing balances.
The Balancer linear pool has 10.055365963093765 pDAI registered cash, but its lower-target fee
accounting leaves only approximately 0.055466 pDAI of additional output capacity on this simple
direction at the sampled state. Queries using shares representing 0.01 and 0.05 aDAI succeed. Queries
using shares representing 1 or 100 aDAI, and a query selling one whole waDAI, revert with BAL#001. A
large share exchange rate is therefore not evidence of large executable output. Replenishing or
restructuring liquidity would be a separate action. Earlier large historical flows do not measure present
capacity.
4. Independent current gates
The destination DAI reserve has unbacked mint cap 0, outstanding unbacked balance 0, and 
actual pDAI cash 0 at the pinned block. These are three different fields. A zero cap forbids positive 
mintUnbacked under that state; zero outstanding unbacked does not establish that no historical mint
occurred.
The wrapper's pure conversions succeed, but maxDeposit, maxMint and previewDeposit(1e18) revert with
arithmetic panic 0x11. Its published current implementation computes the remaining supply capacity by
subtracting supplied principal plus treasury accrual, measured at the stored index, from the supply cap.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 323

Here that basis is approximately 450,597,451.148, above the 338,000,000 supply cap. This checked
subtraction explains the observed underflow. The wrapper applies this gate before both underlying and
aT oken deposit paths. Merely transferring existing aDAI to a prospective depositor does not bypass it.
The same wrapper reports previewRedeem(1 waDAI) = 0. Its redemption limit uses underlying Aave cash even
when selecting the aT oken output path. With no cash in the sampled reserve, the reviewed code does
not support treating redeemAsATokens as an automatic escape from that gate. Existing wrapper tokens can
still be exchanged in a funded market that accepts them.
These are current code-and-state conditions, not permanent impossibility claims. Different
configurations, implementations or funded pools require their own validation. Raising only the unbacked
mint cap would not address all the conditions above.
What would resolve each check?
An authorized Pool configurator can enable a positive unbacked mint allowance large enough for the
outstanding balance and proposed issuance. The mint caller must independently hold the required
bridge permission. Calling backUnbacked after a mint cannot cure a cap check that already reverted.
For the wrapper's subtraction, an authorized change could raise the reserve supply cap above its
calculated supplied amount, with headroom for new issuance and accrual. This implementation treats a 
zero supply cap as unlimited and returns unlimited supply capacity before that subtraction. That
differs from the zero unbacked mint cap, which prevents positive Portal issuance. Reducing
outstanding supplied principal sufficiently could also restore capacity, but withdrawals require underlying
liquidity and appropriate claim ownership; no such reduction was performed or assumed.
A separately authorized wrapper implementation change could handle exhausted capacity without
arithmetic panic and reconsider its aT oken-only deposit gate. Clamping the subtraction to zero alone
would make the limit readable but still would not permit positive deposits. Whether a changed wrapper
should admit existing aT okens independently of ordinary supply capacity is a design choice requiring
review, not a property of the current implementation. This study has not established who controls these
configuration or upgrade permissions.
After either configuration or code changes, the entire sequence needs fresh validation. Pool liquidity,
receipt acceptance, conversion rounding and full backing remain independent requirements. A technical
permission change does not create the underlying assets needed to settle the route.
5. What can fit in one block?
Scope Timing conclusion
Existing local receipt purchase and resale Can be composed into one PulseChain transaction when
every call and repayment succeeds
Local mintUnbacked → wrap → swap → backUnbacked Architecturally composable, but the sampled cap and
wrapper gates prevent this proposed route under
unchanged state
A pARB source lock followed by a PulseChain bridge
delivery
Separate execution environments and message/finality
requirements; not one shared atomic EVM transaction
Destination execution after an accepted message, or using
a prefunded relayer
Destination actions may be atomic; earlier source work and
later settlement remain separate
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 324

Transactions merely placed in the same block are not automatically atomic with one another. The
meaningful local guarantee is one transaction that reverts all its calls if any required step fails. Portal
backing in that transaction needs the entire underlying principal and any supplied fee; the liquidity index
cannot fill a settlement shortfall.
6. Exact contracts and reproduction
Contract PulseChain address
pDAI 0x6b175474e89094c44da98b954eedeac495271d0f
V3 aDAI 0x018008bfb33d285247a21d44e50697654f754e63
V3 waDAI 0x098256c06ab24f5655c5506a6488781bd711c14b
Aave V3 Pool 0x87870bca3f3fd6335c3f4ce8392d69350b4fa4e2
Aave oracle 0x54586be62e3c3580375ae3723c145253060ca0c2
DAI price source 0xaed0c38402a5d19df6e4c03f4e2dced6e29c1ee9
aDAI/pDAI PulseX pair 0xc1d1fdd3f2337e75a257a591f34a7644e0c4d06b
waDAI/pDAI PulseX pair 0xa73104df763f216e7e3a7cdc5b7acc4c00c31f4d
DAI Balancer linear pool 0x6667c6fa9f2b3fc1cc8d85320b62703d938e4385
Raw evidence is under artifacts/pulsechain-portal-pricing-20260930/: discovery.json, details.json, oracle-
discovery.json, quotes.json, feed.json and small-cycle.json. These include requests, responses, chain ID,
block hash and repeat block-hash checks. analysis.json records exact derived amounts and hashes of all
six input files. The experiment manifests are Research/experiments/pulsechain_portal_*_20260930.json.
The current aDAI implementation address read from the proxy is 0x7effd7b47bfd17e52fb7559d3f924201b9dbff3d;
its explorer-published source is saved as aDAI_implementation_source.json. The current wrapper
implementation is 0x715d73a88f2f0115d87cfe5e0f25d756b2f9679f; its saved source is artifacts/parb-
validation-20260928/wav3_impl_source.json. Published source was inspected, not independently recompiled. 
pulsex_pair_source.json documents the 29/10,000 swap fee. No V2 aDAI conclusion is inferred from failed
V2 reserve calls or this bounded pair search.
Reproduce the derived figures without network access, choosing a fresh output:
python Research/scripts/analyze_pulsechain_portal_prices.py \
  --evidence artifacts/pulsechain-portal-pricing-20260930 \
  --output artifacts/pulsechain-portal-pricing-check/analysis.json
Related studies: receipt and validator checks (Appendix 49), linear-pool limits (Appendix 16), Portal
settlement accounting (Appendix 17).
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 325
